posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I am looking for a decal for my snowboard and was thinking a holographic decal would be fitting. I don't really want to use the beer, beer and more beer decal I designed so I thought i would do an internet search. I only have found decals cut from holographic foils. Does anyone know of a source for embossed holographic decals?

![Image](http://www.designerinlight.com/holo/B3logo.JPG)

Or perhaps there is a way to make a waterproof hologram I can stick to my board? Can DCG be shot on film? Is Slavich the thinest film in silver halide? Perhaps I could shoot a rainbow in silver halide and back it with mylar...

posts.author: Martin
posts.content_md:
> Or perhaps there is a way to make a waterproof hologram I can stick to my board? Can DCG be shot on film? Is Slavich the thinest film in silver halide? Perhaps I could shoot a rainbow in silver halide and back it with mylar...

You could use:

the traditional optical adhesives etc. to laminate a film between two transparent plastic sheets;

there might be office laminators around that allow for optical quality sealing;

you might also get along with some of the materials Michael used for film mounting (index matching).

Regarding film materials, yes, Slavich is the only option at this moment.

And yes, you can make DCG on those – fixed – silver halide films (though probably not at the brightness levels you'll see on Dinesh's DCG plates).

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: Have you looked at the Holobank? They produce customized holographic stickers from stock imagery by overprinting, unique diecutting and/or recombinations. Talk to Peter Scheir there (he bought the second hologram I sold about 20 years ago!).
